what: Which JOC syntax real streams use, and what the rare branches decode to
method: Whole files, not head clips. The audit scanned three megabytes off the front of fifteen clips and found no sparse matrices and no coarse quantisation at all; a whole-file scan of the same library finds both, in streaming material, tens of thousands of frames in. Where a rare branch occurs is reported too, so a clip that contains it can be cut and run against Dolby's object decoder.

sparse_and_coarse_against_dolby.reference: Dolby Reference Player 3.2.0 gst-plugins, dlbac3dec out-ch-config=21, drc suppressed, start-up delay dropped
reading: Coarse quantisation was already right: the coarse clip sits at 50 to 57 dB against Dolby with no change.

Sparse mode was wrong. On the three frames of real sparse material available the printed reading gives -13,5, -3,2 and +1,1 dB against Dolby's objects, where the frames either side of them sit at 38 to 58 dB.

Two departures from clause 6.6.2's printed pseudo-code fix it. An unselected channel takes the code that dequantises to zero gain (48 coarse, 96 fine) rather than the printed 50 or 100, which dequantise to a gain of 0,4 and pour four of the five downmix channels into every object. And the channel index accumulates from the resolved index of the previous band rather than from the transmitted one.
Both are needed: the off-channel value alone recovers 10 to 19 dB, the index alone recovers nothing because the off-channel error dominates, and together they give 15,5, 49,0 and 65,0 dB.
Frames with no sparse object are bit-identical before and after, and all 33 work streams decode to byte-identical PCM and DAMF.
sparse_and_coarse_against_dolby.superseded_for_sparse_by: evidence/remediation/sparse-differential.json, which measures every sparse frame in the library across four clips and three readings. The figures below are the two-correction state on the two Extraction clips and are kept as the record of what was measured then.

controlled_generation.what: Can the encoder be made to emit the syntax no real stream uses?
controlled_generation.encoder: Dolby Encoding Engine 5.2.1, encode_to_atmos_ddp, from the controlled Atmos master

data_rate_sweep.reading: Every rate gives downmix configuration 3 and one data point. The data rate is the only lever the encoder offers -- its XML has no core-layout or downmix-configuration option at all -- so configurations 1, 2 and 4 cannot be manufactured with the tools on hand.

fast_movement.what: Five objects moving in a circle, one step every half, third, quarter, one and two frames, plus three still ones as controls. Two data points per frame exist for objects that move faster than one update per frame, so this is what should provoke them.
fast_movement.reading: Zero. DEE writes one data point per frame even for an object that moves four times within one. The two-data-point branches cannot be reached from this encoder either.

controlled_generation.what_is_left: For smooth-2 and steep-2 the only evidence available is a unit test against the printed pseudo-code, which proves the implementation matches clause 6.6.5 and not that Dolby agrees with clause 6.6.5. `every_interpolation_branch_matches_pseudocode_6` in oadec-joc restates pseudo-code 6 independently and reads the interpolated matrix back through `reconstruct` with a unit impulse, checking all four branches at every time slot, every channel and three subbands. They stay N/T.
